The underlying record supports the shape even if 12-0 with four UFC fights is a modest sample to credit at 0.80. 65.7% head strike accuracy, 0.98 head strikes absorbed per minute, 100% takedown defence, a +0.41 control differential, three stoppages in four UFC wins. Spann is unchanged at full trust and is the reason the KO number is extreme. His chin sits at −1.42, the worst composite value on the entire card, and his chin damage factor has bottomed out at 0.500 — the model's floor. He has been finished in 85.7% of his losses, carries early vulnerability +0.71, absorbs 2.68 head strikes per minute against a −0.81 differential, and is 35.

The KO threat differential tells the rest, and the override stretched it: +2.26 for Pinto against −0.32 for Spann, comfortably the largest gap of the night. Pinto's 86.9% is 57.7% KO, 4.0% submission, 25.1% decision; Spann's 13.1% is notable in that his best single route remains a 6.1% submission rather than a 4.0% knockout, consistent with a career 45.5% submission finish rate and first-round submissions of Brzeski and Saint Preux. This is still the only fight on the card the model expects to end inside the first round more often than not: Over 1.5 just 47.6% and Over 2.5 32.3%, with 21,350 of 50,000 sims finishing in round one.

matchupAnalysis: The card's second Elo disagreement, and a stark one: Sy is favoured at 79.0% while sitting 111 points BELOW Bukauskas on the ratings (1575 over five divisional fights against 1686 over twelve). The override moved it modestly, 77.8% → 79.0%, with Sy credited at 0.80; the instruction to put Bukauskas at 1.00 was a no-op, since his computed trust was already 1.000 across thirteen fights. The engines remain in near lock-step (GBM 78.6%, hand-tuned 78.2%), so the disagreement here is purely between the outcome-based rating and everything else.

Un-shrinking Sy sharpened an already lopsided physical matchup. Chin +0.80 → +1.05, output +0.77 → +1.01, grappling +0.41 → +0.54, with power the one entry that worsened (−0.30 → −0.39). His reach composite stays at +2.97 — the single highest value of any fighter on this card (210.82 cm against 193.04, a seven-inch gap) and, being a physical measurement, it was never trust-scaled in the first place. Bukauskas is the more experienced fighter and fully observed, but the observation is bleak: chin −1.15, a chin damage factor of 0.524 barely off the floor, finished in 80% of his losses, early vulnerability +0.66, and a third-round KO loss to Nikita Krylov in January.

The KO threat spread is now the widest structural gap of the night bar Pinto's: Sy +1.11 against Bukauskas −2.00. Two things still cut against the projection and belong on the record. Sy is 1-2 in his last three and lost most recently by first-round submission to Ion Cutelaba — and Bukauskas beat that same Cutelaba by decision, a common opponent pointing the wrong way for the favourite. And Sy remains the less-observed of the two even at 0.80. Method reads 35.5% Sy KO against a 46.4% total decision rate, with the O/U engines agreeing unusually tightly (48.9% vs 49.4%) on a coin-flip at Over 2.5, 49.3%.

It is the card's largest physical edge (reach +2.97, seven inches, never trust-scaled) against its second-worst durability profile: Bukauskas at chin −1.15, damage factor 0.524, finished in 80% of his losses. KO threat +1.11 against −2.00. Against it: Sy is 1-2 in his last three, was submitted in round one by Cutelaba, and Bukauskas beat that same Cutelaba. Distance is a coin-flip (Over 2.5 at 49.3%).
